newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mir station commander's heart condition better.
newsitem.headline: Mir station commander's heart condition better.

text.p: Medical tests show the heart condition of the Russian commander of the troubled space station Mir is getting better, a duty officer at Mission Control said on Monday.
"The electrocardiogram showed that Vasily Tsibliyev's heart condition is improving," the officer told Reuters at the space centre just outside Moscow.
Mission Control officials said on Sunday Tsibliyev's health was gradually "normalising". He underwent a further series of medical tests later on Sunday.

Tsibliyev complained of an irregular heartbeat last week, two weeks after a failed docking manoeuvre in which the Spektr science module attached to Mir was holed and the space station's power supply was damaged.

The crew, which also includes Russian flight engineer Alexander Lazutkin and British-born NASA physicist Michael Foale, fixed their latest problem on Friday by restoring Mir's orientation -- lost when a computer crashed because one of the men mistakenly pulled out a cable.
Space officials have delayed risky repairs to fix the power supply and have made clear they are likely to leave the repairs to a crew which is due to arrive on Mir on August 7.
The final announcement on the repair plans was expected to be made on Monday during a meeting of senior space officials and Mir designers, officials said.
Nadezhda Zaryalova, a flight control spokeswoman, told Reuters the meeting was due to start at 10 a.m. (0600 GMT) and would last until midday.
